title: debark build job v1
description: debark.buildjob/v1 - the job model that keeps the resolution/build engine callable by something other than the CLI: BuildRequest in, BuildResult out. Neither document is ever written into a bundle; both are wire/API objects a caller (the CLI today, a scheduler later) exchanges with the engine. A document validating against this schema is exactly one of the two shapes below, never a mix of their fields.

snapshot_ref.description: Path to a snapshot archive or an already-extracted snapshot directory, resolved by the caller before the engine sees it.

inputs.description: What the operator asked for: packages, URLs, files and directories.

options.description: Knobs that change what apt is asked and what is written.

output.description: Where the bundle goes and how it is signed.

list_files.description: packages.txt-style list files that were expanded into the fields above; recorded for provenance.

url.description: https:// URL of a vendor .deb file.

sha256.description: Operator-supplied expected digest. When present, this file's publisher_verification is upgraded from url-unverified to user-digest.

recommends.description: Overrides the target's apt.conf Install-Recommends. Absent means follow the target's own setting.

upgrades.description: Adds a full-upgrade pass for packages already installed on the target.

update_mode.description: additive (default) adds what is missing and touches nothing else; refresh (--update) re-resolves, re-fetches and then prunes.

prune.description: Removes superseded files in refresh mode. User-supplied files are never pruned regardless of this value.

arch_override.description: Resolve for a different architecture than the snapshot's.

mirror_overrides.description: Maps an original URI prefix to a replacement, for an internal mirror. Recorded in the lock.

backend.description: Which apt runs the resolution. auto picks local or container at request time; the lock never records auto (see lock.v1's resolver.backend).

image.description: Overrides the container image for the container backend.

policy_ref.description: Path to a local debark.policy/v1 file.

approved_keys_ref.description: Path to an organisation-approved archive key fingerprint list that resolution must satisfy.

acknowledge_redistribution.description: Suppresses the interactive redistribution prompt. The warnings are still recorded regardless.

embed_binary.description: Path to a debark target binary to copy into the bundle.

closed_world_check.description: Runs the pre-export offline resolution proof. Defaults to true; only a debugging flag turns it off.

format.description: Shape of the produced bundle: a directory tree, or a single tar.zst archive.

sign.description: Signer selection. Always present in the emitted JSON, possibly as an empty object: encoding/json's omitempty has no effect on a non-pointer struct field (see docs/formats.md).

signer_ref.description: Names the key: a path to an ed25519 private key, gpg:<keyid>, or plugin:<name>.

required.description: Fails the build when signing is impossible. When false and no signer is configured, the bundle is written unsigned and the fact is recorded.

repo_signer_ref.description: Optionally signs the apt Release with a GPG key the target already trusts, producing InRelease/Release.gpg.

signed.description: True when at least one signature block was written.

stats.description: Summary printed after the build and recorded in the lock.

fetch_failed.description: External inputs that did not make it into the bundle: a URL that could not be downloaded, or a local .deb that could not be read. Each entry is the operator's literal input string, and says which input failed, never why. fetch_failures carries the reason, with one entry per entry here, in the same order.

fetch_failures.description: fetch_failed with the reason attached. Added as an optional field under the additive allowance in docs/formats.md 3.6; fetch_failed is deliberately not widened in place, because turning an array of string into an array of object is a meaning change and would force debark.buildjob/v2 on every existing consumer.

exit_class.description: Outcome class; mirrors core/dferr.Class as a stable string so a caller that never sees the process exit code still learns the outcome.

input.description: The operator's literal input string: a URL, or a local .deb path. Matches the corresponding entry in fetch_failed exactly, so the two can be joined. Deliberately not redacted, for the same reason fetch_failed is not - this is operator-facing summary data returned from the engine, never an artefact that ships inside the bundle, and the operator typed this string themselves and has to recognise it to retry.

reason.description: Machine-readable classification; mirrors api/buildjob/v1.FetchFailureReasons() exactly. Each member maps to a distinct operator action, which is the test for adding one. Reasons are additive, so a reader must have a default arm and should treat an unknown value as "other".

detail.description: One-line human explanation, already passed through core/fetch.RedactMessage so it is safe to print, log and store. Absent when the reason says everything there is to say.

added.description: Files newly added to the bundle by this run.

unchanged.description: Files already present and untouched by this run.

bytes.description: Total bytes in the resulting bundle pool.

downloaded_bytes.description: Bytes that actually crossed the network this run.

package_count.description: Number of packages in the resulting bundle.

duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock duration of the build, when measured.
